title: Excel for engineering calculations
why: Engineers use spreadsheets every day for design checks, quantities and quick calculations that sit between hand calcs and specialist software.
what_is_different: Engineering spreadsheets must carry units, cite the design code clause, be checkable by another engineer, and fail loudly when an input is out of range. They are calculation documents, not just tables.

extra_modules.title: Verification and QA
extra_modules.outcome: You can: prove your spreadsheet is right

starter_project: Build a checked calculation workbook for a common design task in your discipline (for example, a retaining-wall stability check or a pipe-sizing calculation) with units, code references and a verification sheet.
pitfalls: No reference to the design code version
Trusting a downloaded spreadsheet without verifying it
Circular references used instead of proper iteration
